slides.title: How far can your skates lean?
slides.sub: Mounting cups, blade height and a solid mount

slides.title: What a mounting cup does
slides.body: Cups set your blade height, set the offset to the left of the boot centre line, and hold the whole assembly rigid through every push.

slides.title: Why taller cups lean deeper
slides.caption: A taller cup lifts the boot away from the ice so you can drop deeper into the corner.

slides.title: Start low and earn the height
slides.body: Taller cups add leverage before a beginner has the ankle strength to use it. Lower cups feel planted and easy to control.

slides.title: Read the engraving, write it down
slides.body: The number on the cup is its height in millimetres. Note front and rear heights so you can repeat a setup that works.

slides.title: Measure bolt spacing before you buy
slides.body: Boots and hardware use set bolt spacings: 165 mm is common on short track boots, 195 mm on inline. If they differ, use an adapter, not a drill.

slides.title: Check your mount every session
slides.body: Try to twist the blade before you lace up, and check each bolt with the Allen key once a month.
